medical_uses: Treats severe diarrhea, dysentery, and helps in the detoxification of insect bites. Boosts cardiovascular health.
treatment_methods: Consume the raw fruit pulp with salt or sugar for digestive issues, or use the crushed leaves to treat skin irritations.
care_instructions: Hardy and drought-tolerant. Prefers full sun and a hot climate. Grows well in sandy or loamy well-draining soil.

description: A beautiful evergreen shrub with clusters of fragrant flowers. Known to be highly toxic if handled improperly.
medical_uses: Used in extremely small, processed doses for heart conditions and skin diseases like leprosy and ringworm.
treatment_methods: WARNING: Highly toxic. Used strictly under medical supervision. Medicated oils are prepared for topical application on chronic skin patches.
care_instructions: Thrives in full sun and heat. Very drought-tolerant. Handle with gloves and keep away from children and pets.

description: An aquatic plant with beautiful white flowers that bloom at night, known for its cooling properties.
medical_uses: Cools the body, treats diarrhea with blood, manages anxiety, and improves heart health.
treatment_methods: The dried petals or rhizomes are boiled to make a decoction, often taken with sugar to reduce body heat.
care_instructions: Aquatic plant. Requires a pond or large water container. Needs full sun and heavy clay soil under water.

description: A tall perennial herb found in the alpine regions of the Himalayas, valued for its highly aromatic roots.
medical_uses: Treats chronic skin diseases, asthma, and chronic cough. Improves digestion and relieves abdominal pain.
treatment_methods: The dried root is powdered and used as a paste for skin issues or consumed with honey for respiratory relief.
care_instructions: Requires high-altitude, cold climates. Needs moist, deep, loamy soil rich in organic matter.

description: A stunning climbing lily with flame-like flowers. Its tuberous roots are highly potent and toxic in raw form.
medical_uses: Used to induce labor (historically), treat piles, and expel parasitic worms. Highly valued for treating snake bites.
treatment_methods: WARNING: Highly toxic. Used only after rigorous purification. Root paste is applied topically for skin issues or joint pain.
care_instructions: Needs a trellis for climbing. Requires warm, humid conditions and well-drained, fertile soil.

description: A perennial herb whose roots are incredibly sweet and famous worldwide for their soothing properties.
medical_uses: Instantly soothes sore throats and coughs. Heals gastric ulcers, improves skin complexion, and acts as an anti-inflammatory.
treatment_methods: Chew on a piece of the dried root for throat relief, or boil it in water to make a medicinal tea for the stomach.
care_instructions: Requires a long growing season in full sun. Needs deep, well-draining sandy loam soil to allow roots to develop.

description: A fast-growing deciduous tree similar to Neem, with beautiful lilac-colored, fragrant flowers.
medical_uses: Treats skin diseases, expels intestinal worms, and reduces systemic inflammation. The leaves are used for joint pain.
treatment_methods: The leaf paste is applied to skin eruptions, and the bark decoction is used in controlled doses for deworming.
care_instructions: Highly adaptable and fast-growing. Prefers full sun and well-drained soil. Very drought-resistant.

description: A small perennial herb with tuberous roots, regarded as a vital 'Rasayana' (rejuvenative) herb in Ayurveda.
medical_uses: Boosts physical strength and fertility, treats urinary issues, and acts as a potent immunomodulator.
treatment_methods: The roots are dried and powdered, then consumed with warm milk and honey for rejuvenation.
care_instructions: Requires a hot and humid climate. Grows well in partial shade with moist, fertile soil.

description: A common citrus tree whose fruit is an indispensable part of Indian medicine and culinary practices.
medical_uses: Highest natural source of Vitamin C. Improves digestion, clears skin, aids weight loss, and prevents scurvy.
treatment_methods: Drink fresh lemon juice in warm water on an empty stomach for detoxification and metabolic boost.
care_instructions: Requires at least 8 hours of full sun. Plant in well-draining soil and water consistently during fruiting.

description: A beautiful tree from the Himalayas, whose fragrant wood and bark are used as a cooling tonic.
medical_uses: Cools the body, treats skin diseases, reduces burning sensations, and promotes wound healing.
treatment_methods: The wood is ground into a paste for topical skin application, or the bark is boiled into a decoction.
care_instructions: Requires temperate climates with cool winters. Thrives in well-drained soil and full sun to partial shade.

description: A small, delicate annual herb with finely divided leaves, found commonly in the cultivated fields of North India.
medical_uses: The premier herb for treating fevers, especially those associated with burning sensations. Purifies blood and treats skin diseases.
treatment_methods: The whole plant is boiled to make a cooling decoction, often taken to reduce high body temperature and clear toxins.
care_instructions: Requires cool weather and moist soil. Grows easily as a seasonal weed in full sun to partial shade.

description: A beautiful shrub with large, velvety leaves and clusters of bright purple berries.
medical_uses: Cools the body, stops internal bleeding, and treats skin conditions like prickly heat and rashes.
treatment_methods: The dried flowers or fruit powder is consumed with honey to cool the system or applied topically for skin relief.
care_instructions: Requires a tropical or subtropical climate. Grows well in rich, moist soil with partial shade.

description: A deciduous tree known as the 'Desert Teak', yielding beautiful orange-yellow flowers.
medical_uses: Highly effective for liver and spleen disorders, including jaundice and an enlarged spleen (splenomegaly).
treatment_methods: The bark is dried and boiled into a decoction to support hepatobiliary health and reduce organ swelling.
care_instructions: Extremely drought-tolerant. Requires full sun and well-drained sandy or rocky soil.

description: An evergreen tree with leaves arranged in whorls of seven, commonly known as the 'Devil's Tree'.
medical_uses: Traditionally used to treat malaria, chronic skin diseases, and malabsorption syndrome.
treatment_methods: The bark decoction is taken in small doses for fever. The milky latex is applied to skin ulcers for healing.
care_instructions: Hardy and fast-growing. Prefers full sun and moderate watering. Grows well in various soil types.

description: A medium-sized tree producing small, slimy, edible fruits known as Indian Cherry or Lasora.
medical_uses: Treats chronic coughs, asthma, and digestive issues. The fruit is highly nutritious and acts as a natural demulcent.
treatment_methods: Eat the ripe fruit for respiratory relief. The bark decoction is used for washing skin wounds.
care_instructions: Thrives in dry deciduous forests. Needs full sun and well-draining soil. Requires minimal watering once established.

description: A large succulent shrub with thorny, jointed stems, often used in rural India as a living hedge.
medical_uses: Used for severe constipation and to treat piles (Kshara Sutra therapy). The latex is a potent purgative.
treatment_methods: WARNING: The latex is caustic. Used strictly in professional Ayurvedic surgical procedures for treating fistulas and piles.
care_instructions: Treat like a cactus. Requires full sun and exceptionally well-draining soil. Very drought-resistant.

description: A large perennial climber with milky juice, commonly known as 'Indian Rhubarb'.
medical_uses: Regarded as one of the best and safest herbs for purgation (Virechana). Treats edema, jaundice, and piles.
treatment_methods: The root bark is dried and powdered, taken in small doses with warm water or milk for systemic cleansing.
care_instructions: Requires a trellis or support for climbing. Needs full sun and well-drained, loamy soil.

description: A parasitic shrub that grows on the branches of other trees, such as Mango or Neem trees.
medical_uses: Used to treat kidney stones, asthma, and to speed up the healing of deep wounds and fractures.
treatment_methods: The leaves are boiled to make a decoction, taken internally for urinary issues or applied as a wash for skin ulcers.
care_instructions: A parasitic plant that requires a host tree to survive. Not suitable for standard garden cultivation.

description: A deciduous tree found along riverbanks, recognized for its efficacy in treating urinary disorders.
medical_uses: The premier herb for breaking down kidney stones (lithotriptic) and treating prostate enlargement.
treatment_methods: The bark decoction is taken daily to flush the urinary tract and prevent stone formation.
care_instructions: Prefers moist, alluvial soil near water sources. Needs full sun to partial shade and regular watering.

description: A climbing shrub with small berries that resemble black pepper, known as 'False Black Pepper'.
medical_uses: The most powerful Ayurvedic herb for expelling intestinal worms. Also treats indigestion and improves skin health.
treatment_methods: The dried berries are powdered and consumed with honey or warm water, particularly for children with worms.
care_instructions: Requires a tropical or subtropical climate. Grows best in partial shade with rich, well-draining forest soil.

description: A vigorous climbing vine with large, heart-shaped leaves that are silvery-white on the underside.
medical_uses: Acts as a powerful brain tonic, improves memory, treats arthritis, and boosts physical stamina.
treatment_methods: The root powder is consumed with warm milk as a rejuvenating tonic or applied topically for joint pain.
care_instructions: Needs a strong support structure for climbing. Thrives in full sun to partial shade in moist, fertile soil.

description: One of the most ancient grains cultivated in India, widely used as both food and medicine.
medical_uses: Highly effective for managing diabetes, reducing obesity, and treating urinary tract infections.
treatment_methods: Consume barley water (boiling barley in water) to flush the kidneys or use barley flour in the daily diet for weight loss.
care_instructions: Cool-season crop. Requires full sun and well-drained loamy soil. Relatively drought-tolerant.

description: A large evergreen tree bearing large, acidic fruits, found primarily in the northeastern regions of India.
medical_uses: Supports heart health, improves digestion, and acts as a natural souring agent to clear systemic blockages.
treatment_methods: The dried fruit slices are soaked in water to make a tart medicinal drink or used in small quantities in cooking.
care_instructions: Requires a humid, tropical climate and rich, moist soil. Grows best in partial shade to full sun.

description: A perennial herb found in the alpine Himalayas, known for its non-toxic, highly medicinal roots.
medical_uses: Treats fevers, acute diarrhea, and digestive disorders in children. Acts as a potent appetizer.
treatment_methods: The dried roots are powdered and taken in small doses with honey for digestive and respiratory relief.
care_instructions: Requires high-altitude, cold climates. Needs moist, rocky, alpine soil. Not suitable for cultivation in the plains.

description: A small shrub cultivated extensively in South India for its powerful laxative properties.
medical_uses: The premier herb for acute constipation and for clearing the bowels before diagnostic procedures.
treatment_methods: The dried leaves or pods are steeped in warm water to make a tea, typically taken at bedtime.
care_instructions: Requires full sun and well-drained, sandy soil. Extremely drought-tolerant and heat-loving.

description: A medium-sized evergreen tree with fragrant white flowers, traditionally used for oral health.
medical_uses: Strengthens loose teeth, treats bleeding gums, and heals skin ulcers. The flowers are used in aromatherapy.
treatment_methods: The bark decoction is used as a mouthwash for oral hygiene. A paste of the bark is applied to skin sores.
care_instructions: Prefers a tropical climate and full sun. Grows slowly in rich, well-draining soil. Requires moderate watering.

description: A large deciduous tree producing nut-like fruits, one of the three ingredients of 'Triphala'.
medical_uses: Treats coughs, asthma, hoarseness of voice, and hair loss. Acts as a potent lung tonic.
treatment_methods: The fruit rind is powdered and consumed with honey for respiratory relief or mixed in hair oils.
care_instructions: Requires full sun and a tropical climate. Adaptable to various soils. Drought-tolerant once mature.

description: A small, creeping herb with three-lobed leaves and a distinct sour taste, found in damp gardens.
medical_uses: Treats chronic indigestion, piles, and helps reduce acidity and heartburn.
treatment_methods: The fresh leaves can be eaten raw in small quantities or their juice extracted for digestive support.
care_instructions: Grows easily in moist, shady garden corners. Requires minimal care and spreads rapidly in damp soil.

description: A resilient, spreading grass considered sacred in India, known for its extreme vitality and cooling nature.
medical_uses: Stops external and internal bleeding, treats skin rashes, and helps manage high blood pressure.
treatment_methods: Extract juice from the fresh grass and apply topically for rashes or consume for internal cooling and bleeding control.
care_instructions: Extremely hardy. Grows in almost any soil and climate. Needs full sun and regular watering for a lush green appearance.

description: A delicate, beautiful fern with crescent-shaped leaflets, often found near waterfalls and damp walls.
medical_uses: Treats skin diseases like erysipelas, heals wounds, and clears respiratory congestion and coughs.
treatment_methods: The whole plant is boiled into a decoction or applied as a paste to skin eruptions for fast healing.
care_instructions: Requires high humidity and shade. Plant in well-draining, moist soil and protect from direct sunlight.

description: The common sugarcane, regarded in Ayurveda as a highly nutritious and tissue-building medicine.
medical_uses: Treats jaundice, provides instant energy, strengthens the liver, and helps with urinary retention.
treatment_methods: Drink fresh sugarcane juice daily to support liver recovery and maintain hydration and energy levels.
care_instructions: Requires a tropical climate with high humidity and full sun. Needs rich, moist soil and heavy watering.

description: A climbing vine bearing distinctively bitter, bumpy green fruits, a staple medicinal vegetable in India.
medical_uses: The premier natural remedy for managing diabetes. Also purifies blood and treats skin diseases.
treatment_methods: Drink fresh bitter gourd juice on an empty stomach to lower blood sugar levels and improve metabolic health.
care_instructions: Needs a trellis for climbing. Thrives in full sun and rich, well-draining soil with regular watering.

description: A small annual shrub with yellow flowers and long pods, commonly known as 'Negro Coffee'.
medical_uses: Treats asthma, chronic coughs, and skin infections. Helps clear the respiratory tract of excess mucus.
treatment_methods: The leaves and seeds are boiled to make a decoction for respiratory relief or applied as a paste for skin issues.
care_instructions: Grows easily in tropical wastelands. Needs full sun and well-draining soil. Requires very little water.

description: A beautiful tree with orchid-like purple flowers and twin-lobed leaves, similar to Kanchanar.
medical_uses: Regulates thyroid function, treats swollen glands, and heals skin ulcers and acne.
treatment_methods: The bark is boiled to make a decoction for thyroid support or used as a wash for skin conditions.
care_instructions: Prefers full sun and moderate watering. Adaptable to various soil types, provided they are well-draining.

description: A spiny, climbing shrub producing grey, marble-like seeds known as 'Fever Nuts'.
medical_uses: Highly effective for treating fevers, malaria, and severe abdominal inflammation and pain.
treatment_methods: The seeds are crushed and powdered, usually taken with honey or water to reduce fever and inflammation.
care_instructions: Needs a strong support structure for climbing. Thrives in tropical areas with full sun and well-drained soil.

description: Galls formed on oak trees by insects, exceptionally rich in tannins and highly astringent.
medical_uses: Treats severe oral issues like bleeding gums and loose teeth. Also stops diarrhea and vaginal discharges.
treatment_methods: The powdered galls are used as a tooth powder for gum health or boiled to make a gargle for sore throats.
care_instructions: Requires temperate climates to grow oak trees. The galls are harvested from the trees during the appropriate season.

description: A creeping annual or perennial herb with three-lobed leaves, valued as a tissue-building herb.
medical_uses: Strengthens the body, treats liver disorders, and acts as a potent antioxidant and rejuvenator.
treatment_methods: The whole plant is boiled to make a decoction or consumed in powdered form to build physical stamina.
care_instructions: Grows well in open grasslands. Requires full sun and moderately moist, well-draining soil.

description: A small, aromatic annual herb with spherical, purple flower heads, commonly found in harvested rice fields.
medical_uses: Boosts immunity, treats skin diseases, and manages respiratory conditions like asthma and chronic cough.
treatment_methods: The flower heads are dried and powdered, taken with honey to improve systemic immunity and clear skin.
care_instructions: Requires moist soil and full sun. Grows easily in tropical plains after the monsoon season.

description: A small tree producing tiny, purple, sweet-and-sour berries known as Phalsa.
medical_uses: Cools the body instantly, provides high energy, and treats anemia and burning sensations.
treatment_methods: Drink fresh Phalsa juice in summer to prevent heatstroke and provide a natural electrolyte boost.
care_instructions: Loves hot summers and full sun. Needs well-drained soil. Drought-tolerant but needs water during fruiting.

description: A large deciduous tree with fragrant, bell-shaped flowers, another of the 'Dashamoola' roots.
medical_uses: Potent anti-inflammatory used for joint pain, respiratory infections, and to improve heart health.
treatment_methods: The root bark is used to prepare decoctions, often combined with other roots to treat systemic inflammation.
care_instructions: Thrives in dry forests. Requires full sun and deep, well-draining soil. Drought-resistant once mature.

description: A large shrub or small tree whose wood, when rubbed together, traditionally generates fire.
medical_uses: An important ingredient in Dashamoola. Treats neuralgia, swelling, arthritis, and supports deep nerve healing.
treatment_methods: The root bark is boiled into a decoction to reduce inflammation and nervous system pain.
care_instructions: Requires full sun and well-drained soil. Hardy and drought-resistant in tropical climates.

description: A deciduous tree producing sour, plum-like fruits used in pickles and traditional cooking.
medical_uses: Relieves severe earaches, treats diarrhea, and acts as a potent astringent for internal bleeding.
treatment_methods: The juice of the bark is dropped into the ear for pain, while the fruit is consumed for digestive health.
care_instructions: Thrives in tropical regions. Needs full sun and deep, loamy soil with regular watering.

description: A thorny, deciduous tree found in the dry regions of India.
medical_uses: Historically known as the primary antidote for dog bites (rabies). Treats severe skin diseases and arthritis.
treatment_methods: The root bark powder is consumed in tiny, strictly supervised doses or applied as an oil for joint pain.
care_instructions: Extremely drought-tolerant. Prefers dry, rocky, and sandy soils with full sun.

description: A striking climbing vine with vivid, deep blue flowers shaped like a conch shell.
medical_uses: A powerful brain tonic (Medhya Rasayana). Enhances memory, treats anxiety, and relieves chronic migraines.
treatment_methods: The blue flowers are steeped in hot water to make a color-changing, antioxidant-rich, brain-boosting tea.
care_instructions: Needs a trellis for support. Prefers full sun to partial shade and moist, well-draining soil.

description: A large, wild-growing shrub producing a highly caustic, milky white latex when cut.
medical_uses: Treats severe asthma, clears respiratory blockages, and heals ringworm and leprosy.
treatment_methods: WARNING: Highly toxic latex. The processed root bark is used for asthma, while the latex is applied only externally to warts.
care_instructions: Grows wild in barren, dry lands. Requires intense sun and sandy soil. Needs no additional watering.

description: A prickly, low-growing perennial shrub, one of the ten roots of the Dashamoola formula.
medical_uses: Relieves chest congestion, treats asthma, soothes a sore throat, and reduces systemic inflammation.
treatment_methods: The roots and fruits are boiled into a decoction to clear the lungs and reduce fever.
care_instructions: Grows easily in tropical climates. Thrives in full sun and well-drained, sandy loam.

description: A large evergreen tree famed for its intensely fragrant, golden-yellow flowers.
medical_uses: Reduces fever, relieves burning sensations, stops nausea, and treats severe headaches.
treatment_methods: The highly aromatic flowers are steeped in water or distilled to relieve stress and internal heat.
care_instructions: Requires a humid, tropical environment. Needs deep, rich, moist soil and partial shade when young.

description: A spreading shrub that blooms with brilliant red, tubular flowers.
medical_uses: The essential catalyst in Ayurveda for fermenting herbal wines (Asavas and Arishtas). Also stops diarrhea.
treatment_methods: The dried flowers are added to herbal decoctions to initiate fermentation and extract active plant compounds.
care_instructions: Hardy and drought-resistant. Prefers full sun and grows well in rocky, dry soils.

description: A hardy, drought-resistant shrub producing small, edible, astringent berries.
medical_uses: Treats severe diarrhea, strengthens the body during recovery from illness, and heals bone fractures.
treatment_methods: The berries are eaten raw, or the bark is boiled into a strengthening decoction.
care_instructions: Extremely drought-tolerant. Thrives in hot, arid deserts and rocky terrains.

description: An unusual plant with enormous, elephant-ear-shaped leaves.
medical_uses: Provides immense physical strength, treats joint pain, and heals deep, non-healing wounds.
treatment_methods: The tuberous roots are powdered and taken with milk for vitality, or the large leaves are applied to wounds.

description: An annual flowering plant known for its black seeds, often referred to as 'black cumin'.
medical_uses: Boosts immunity, treats asthma, lowers blood pressure, and promotes hair growth.
treatment_methods: Consume the seeds daily or apply cold-pressed black seed oil to the skin and scalp.
care_instructions: Prefers full sun and rich, well-draining soil. Requires regular watering during the growing season.

description: A small tree that blooms with intensely fragrant white flowers with orange stems, which fall at dawn.
medical_uses: Treats sciatica, arthritis, chronic fevers (like malaria), and acts as a mild laxative.
treatment_methods: Boil the leaves into a strong decoction to relieve sciatic nerve pain and joint inflammation.
care_instructions: Needs a tropical climate, full sun to partial shade, and well-draining soil.

description: A small to medium-sized deciduous tree with massive compound leaves and large, sword-like seed pods.
medical_uses: A key ingredient in 'Dashamoola'. Treats diarrhea, dysentery, joint pain, and asthma.
treatment_methods: The root bark is boiled into a decoction for internal use or applied as a paste on swollen joints.
care_instructions: Thrives in moist, deciduous forests. Prefers full sun and well-drained loamy soil.

description: An erect, annual herb recognized for its tiny, dark brown seeds.
medical_uses: The primary Ayurvedic remedy for vitiligo, psoriasis, and leprosy.
treatment_methods: The seed powder or oil is applied directly to the depigmented skin, followed by brief sun exposure.
care_instructions: Requires full sun, warm temperatures, and well-draining sandy loam. Drought tolerant.

description: A large deciduous tree known as the Indian Kino Tree, whose wood and resin are highly medicinal.
medical_uses: Excellent for managing diabetes, reducing cholesterol, and treating skin diseases.
treatment_methods: Water stored overnight in tumblers made of its wood is consumed in the morning to lower blood sugar.
care_instructions: Requires tropical climates, full sun, and well-draining soil. Can grow very large.

description: A large, thorny, deciduous shrub or small tree bearing round, yellowish fruits.
medical_uses: The premier herb used for inducing vomiting (Vamana therapy) in Panchakarma detoxification.
treatment_methods: The fruit powder is administered with honey and rock salt specifically to induce therapeutic emesis.
care_instructions: Extremely hardy. Grows in dry, deciduous forests in full sun and poor soils.

description: A perennial subshrub with heart-shaped leaves, renowned for its strength-giving properties.
medical_uses: Treats nervous disorders, asthma, weight loss, and builds muscle strength and stamina.
treatment_methods: The root and leaves are boiled with milk or made into medicated massage oils (e.g., Mahanarayan Taila).
care_instructions: Grows wild as a weed. Prefers full sun and well-draining sandy or loamy soils.

description: A climbing, woody vine with prickly stems and tuberous roots.
medical_uses: Treats syphilis, gout, rheumatoid arthritis, and chronic skin diseases.
treatment_methods: The tuberous roots are dried, powdered, and consumed as a decoction or with honey.
care_instructions: Requires partial shade, moist, rich, and well-draining soil, along with a trellis for climbing.

description: A strongly scented, spreading aromatic herb with distinct globose, purple flower heads.
medical_uses: Treats gout, enlarged spleen, skin diseases, and acts as a general nervine tonic.
treatment_methods: The whole plant or the flower heads are dried and consumed as a powder or decoction.
care_instructions: A weed of damp places and paddy fields. Thrives in moist, waterlogged clay soils.

description: A medium-sized tree bearing fruit resembling small oranges, containing highly toxic, disk-shaped seeds.
medical_uses: A powerful nerve stimulant. Treats paralysis, neuralgia, and chronic dyspepsia.
treatment_methods: Extremely toxic. Seeds must undergo rigorous purification (Shodhana) before use in minute, prescribed doses.
care_instructions: Requires a hot, tropical climate. Thrives in full sun and well-draining laterite soils.

description: An annual or biennial herb native to the Himalayas, known for its intense bitterness.
medical_uses: Treats chronic fevers, liver disorders, malaria, and improves appetite.
treatment_methods: The whole plant is soaked in water overnight, and the extremely bitter infusion is consumed the next morning.
care_instructions: Requires cool, high-altitude climates. Plant in moist, well-draining, humus-rich soil.

description: A highly branched, sub-erect herbaceous perennial that grows widely as a wasteland weed.
medical_uses: The best herb for treating an enlarged spleen, liver disorders, and chronic wounds.
treatment_methods: The root is chewed or boiled into a decoction for spleen and liver health.
care_instructions: Grows vigorously in dry, sandy, or rocky soils. Highly drought-tolerant and requires full sun.

description: A climbing, herbaceous vine with heart-shaped leaves, renowned as the 'root of immortality'.
medical_uses: A supreme immunomodulator. Treats dengue, malaria, chronic fevers, diabetes, and arthritis.
treatment_methods: The stem is crushed and boiled to make a potent decoction, often taken with ginger and honey.
care_instructions: Requires a support tree (like Neem for added potency), full sun to partial shade, and moderate watering.

description: An annual plant cultivated worldwide; its seeds and leaves are staples in Indian cooking.
medical_uses: Lowers blood sugar, improves milk production in nursing mothers, and reduces menstrual discomfort.
treatment_methods: Soak seeds overnight and drink the water. Use leaves fresh in cooking or dry for later use.
care_instructions: Requires full sun and well-draining, slightly acidic soil. Cool weather crop.

description: An erect, little-branched perennial herb with distinctive variegated leaves and dense, cylindrical flower spikes.
medical_uses: A key ingredient in 'Dashamoola'. Treats asthma, heart disease, bleeding disorders, and fractures.
treatment_methods: The whole plant, particularly the root, is boiled to make a strengthening decoction.
care_instructions: Prefers tropical climates, well-draining loamy soils, and full sun to partial shade.

description: A perennial herb native to the Himalayas, yielding a highly aromatic rhizome used as a sedative.
medical_uses: Treats insomnia, anxiety, epilepsy, and acts as a potent nervine relaxant.
treatment_methods: The dried root powder is consumed with warm milk before bed or used in aromatherapy.
care_instructions: Requires high altitudes, cool temperatures, partial shade, and moist, rich soil.

description: A much-branched, highly spreading shrub known for its brilliant, tubular red flowers.
medical_uses: Treats severe diarrhea, dysentery, bleeding disorders, and acts as a fermentation agent in Ayurvedic wines (Asavas).
treatment_methods: The dried flowers are powdered and taken with honey, or added to herbal decoctions to initiate fermentation.
care_instructions: Extremely hardy. Thrives in full sun, rocky, well-draining soils, and dry climates.

description: A flowering plant whose rhizome, ginger root, is a universally used spice and folk medicine.
medical_uses: Treats nausea, motion sickness, osteoarthritis, indigestion, and chronic coughs.
treatment_methods: Crush fresh ginger into tea, chew it with salt before meals, or use dried powder (Shunthi) in formulas.
care_instructions: Requires hot, humid climates, partial shade, and rich, consistently moist, well-draining soil.

description: A trailing weed known to 'rejuvenate' the body, featuring small pink flowers and sticky seeds.
medical_uses: A powerful diuretic. Treats kidney disorders, edema (swelling), anemia, and urinary tract infections.
treatment_methods: The whole plant is dried and consumed as a decoction, or the fresh leaves are cooked as a vegetable.
care_instructions: A highly resilient weed. Thrives in full sun and almost any soil type. Needs very little water.

description: A small shrub native to the Arabian Peninsula and India, recognized for its yellow flowers and flat seed pods.
medical_uses: An FDA-approved nonprescription laxative. Used to treat severe constipation and clear the bowel before diagnostic tests.
treatment_methods: The dried leaves or pods are brewed into a tea. Must be used short-term to avoid dependency.
care_instructions: Requires hot, dry climates, full sun, and well-draining sandy soils. Highly drought-tolerant.

description: A small, herbaceous, frost-tender perennial plant that grows creeping along the ground in swampy areas.
medical_uses: The ultimate brain food. Enhances memory, heals wounds, treats varicose veins, and reduces anxiety.
treatment_methods: Eat fresh leaves in salads, extract the juice, or brew dried leaves into a restorative tea.
care_instructions: Needs high moisture and humidity. Grow in partial shade in continuously moist, boggy soil.

description: A small, hairy, perennial herb with beautiful, tiny, sky-blue, funnel-shaped flowers.
medical_uses: A powerful brain tonic. Enhances cognitive function, reduces stress, treats epilepsy, and induces sleep.
treatment_methods: The entire plant is dried, powdered, and consumed with warm milk or made into a medicated syrup.
care_instructions: Grows wild in open, grassy areas. Prefers full sun and well-draining, sandy or rocky soils.

description: A slender, twining, aromatic shrub known for its sweet-smelling roots that resemble the scent of vanilla.
medical_uses: Purifies the blood, treats skin diseases like eczema, acts as a coolant, and manages autoimmune disorders.
treatment_methods: Boil the dried roots to make a fragrant herbal tea or decoction, often consumed during hot summers.
care_instructions: Thrives in partial shade to full sun. Requires well-drained, sandy loam soil. Moderately drought-tolerant.

description: A vigorous climbing legume known for the extreme itchiness caused by the hairs on its seed pods.
medical_uses: A natural source of L-DOPA. Used for Parkinson's disease, nervous disorders, and male infertility.
treatment_methods: The seeds are strictly processed and powdered, typically consumed with milk. Great care must be taken to avoid the irritating pod hairs.
care_instructions: Requires a tropical climate, full sun, and a trellis for support. Plant in well-drained, sandy loam soil.

description: A widespread tropical weed characterized by small, round leaves arranged in rows with tiny fruits hidden underneath.
medical_uses: Highly effective for liver disorders including Hepatitis B, jaundice, and helps break down kidney stones.
treatment_methods: Crush the entire fresh plant to extract juice, or use dried plant powder boiled as a decoction.
care_instructions: Grows easily in tropical environments. Prefers partial shade and moist, well-draining soil.

description: An evergreen shrub with whorled leaves and small, pinkish-white flowers, famous as the source of reserpine.
medical_uses: A powerful tranquilizer used to treat severe high blood pressure, insomnia, and psychiatric disorders.
treatment_methods: The roots are dried and ground. Due to its high potency, it must only be taken under strict medical supervision.
care_instructions: Requires a hot, humid climate. Prefers partial shade and deep, fertile, highly organic, well-draining soil.

description: A prickly, low-growing perennial herb bearing bright purple flowers and yellow berries, covered in spines.
medical_uses: A primary herb for respiratory ailments: treats asthma, chronic coughs, chest pain, and bronchitis.
treatment_methods: The entire plant (roots, leaves, berries) is dried and boiled into a decoction, consumed with honey.
care_instructions: Grows wild in dry, arid waste lands. Thrives in full sun and poor, sandy, well-draining soils.

description: A low-growing, creeping plant with thorny fruits, often considered a weed but highly valued in Ayurveda.
medical_uses: Treats urinary tract infections, kidney stones, improves sexual health, and builds muscle strength.
treatment_methods: The dried fruits and roots are powdered and boiled in water to make a decoction, often taken with honey.
care_instructions: Thrives in dry, sandy, and arid environments. Requires full sunlight and very little water.
